history.summary: Ancient temple of Goddess Dindeshwari in Malhar, the archaeological town of Bilaspur district. Sources place it in the 10th–11th century and associate it with the Kalchuri regime; the idol of the goddess is of black granite. NOTE: the CSV town 'Bilaspur' is imprecise — the temple is in Malhar, ~30–40 km south of Bilaspur city (corrected above). Coordinates below are town-level Malhar coordinates (approximate) — the exact temple location is not independently pinpointed. UNVERIFIED: one user review calls this the 51st of 52 Shaktipeeths; this is not corroborated by any authoritative source.

name: Dindeshwari Temple
town_description: Malhar, also known as Saravpur, is an ancient town in Bilaspur district, Chhattisgarh, about 40 km south of Bilaspur city on the Bilaspur–Shivri Narayan road. It was once an important regional centre, visited in antiquity by the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang, and excavations here have revealed remains from the Stone Age through the Satavahana, Kushan and Kalchuri periods. The town is famous for its cluster of ancient temples — Pataleshwar, Deor/Devri and Dindeshwari — and an ASI-recognised archaeological museum housing excavated sculptures.
